### Understanding the Error Function

The **error function**, denoted as \\( erf(x) \\), is a special function that frequently appears in **probability**, **statistics**, and **partial differential equations**.  

It is defined as:  

\[
\operatorname{erf}(x) = \frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}} \int_0^x e^{-t^2} \, dt
\]

This function is closely related to the **cumulative distribution function (CDF)** of the **standard normal distribution**, expressed as:  

\[
\Phi(x) = \frac{1}{2}\left[1 + \operatorname{erf}\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\right].
\]

By rearranging, we can write the error function in terms of the normal CDF:  

\[
\operatorname{erf}(x) = 2 \, \Phi(x \sqrt{2}) - 1.
\]

The error function transitions smoothly from **-1 to 1** and represents **cumulative probability** under the Gaussian curve.  

In the example below, we compute and visualize \\( \operatorname{erf}(x) \\) alongside the corresponding transformation of the standard normal CDF to verify their equivalence.


```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Visualizing and Understanding the Error Function (erf)
# ============================================================

# Description:
# The error function erf(x) is a special function that arises in probability,
# statistics, and partial differential equations. It is defined as:
#     erf(x) = (2 / sqrt(pi)) * ∫₀ˣ e^(-t²) dt
# This function is closely related to the cumulative distribution function (CDF)
# of the standard normal distribution:
#     Φ(x) = (1/2) * [1 + erf(x / sqrt(2))]
# Hence, erf(x) = 2 * Φ(x * sqrt(2)) - 1
#
# The error function transitions smoothly from -1 to 1 and describes cumulative
# probabilities under the Gaussian curve. In this example, we will compute and
# visualize erf(x) alongside the corresponding transformation of the standard
# normal CDF to verify their equivalence.

# Load libraries
library(ggplot2)

# Define the error function using its relationship to the normal CDF
erf <- function(x) {
  2 * pnorm(x * sqrt(2)) - 1
}

# Define a sequence of x-values
x <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 300)

# Compute erf(x) and the normal CDF Phi(x)
data <- data.frame(
  x = x,
  erf = erf(x),
  Phi = pnorm(x)
)

# Plot the error function and its relationship to the normal CDF
ggplot(data, aes(x = x)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = erf, color = "erf(x)"), size = 1.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = 2 * Phi - 1, color = "2Φ(x) - 1"), linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dotted", color = "gray40") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("erf(x)" = "blue", "2Φ(x) - 1" = "red")) +
  labs(
    title = "The Error Function (erf) and its Relation to the Normal CDF",
    subtitle = expression(erf(x) == (2/sqrt(pi)) * integral(e^{-t^2} * dt, 0, x)),
    x = "x",
    y = "Function Value",
    color = "Legend"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

# Interpretation:
# The solid blue line shows the computed error function erf(x),
# while the dashed red line shows the equivalent expression 2Φ(x) - 1,
# where Φ(x) is the standard normal CDF.
# Both curves coincide perfectly, confirming that erf(x) = 2Φ(x√2) - 1.
# The horizontal dotted lines at -1 and +1 indicate the asymptotic limits
# of the error function as x → ±∞.

```
